chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon him), said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The pre-dawn meal (Suhoor) is a blessing.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'My community should not leave the pre-dawn meal, even if it were upon stems (remaining after harvest).'

key_terms.السَّحُورُ: The pre-dawn meal eaten before fasting
key_terms.حَشَفَةٍ: Stems or stalks remaining after harvest, indicating meager food

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the pre-dawn meal (Suhoor) in Shia Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith underscores the pre-dawn meal (Suhoor) as a distinct Sunnah that carries divine blessing (barakah) and serves as a differentiator between Islamic fasting and that of previous nations. The Prophet’s instruction to not neglect it even on 'hashafah' (the remnants of dates or simple sustenance) highlights its spiritual significance over mere physical sustenance, a point emphasized by Shia scholars as a means of following the Prophet’s specific guidance for the Ummah.
